channel.title: Mercury Blog
channel.description: News, engineering notes and field reports from the team building Mercury.

item.title: Mercury Weekly #1: IPOs, models and agents that pay
item.description: The week of 9 to 15 November 2026: Anthropic's IPO roadshow, Nvidia's CEO change, new frontier models, ChatGPT Wallet and the Decisions API.

item.title: What Is a Personal AI Assistant? 10 Real Tasks in 2026
item.description: A personal AI assistant acts for one person across accounts, files, apps and services. What it is, ten tasks it handles, and the permissions each needs.

item.title: 9 AI Agents Compared for Real Work: Memory and Permissions
item.description: Nine AI agents compared on memory, where they run, what they can touch, scheduling, permissions, model choice and price.

item.title: A tour of Mercury Desktop: one app, every Mercury you run
item.description: What's inside Mercury Desktop 1.5.0: chat, research, code, bots, memory and voice, plus connecting to several Mercury servers and keeping them all updated.

item.title: Mercury 1.5: Mercury Desktop
item.description: Mercury 1.5.0 ships Mercury Desktop for macOS, Windows and Linux, remote access the owner approves, and updates that roll back on their own.

item.title: Your agent returned 200 OK. It may still have failed
item.description: What to record in an AI agent run to find its first wrong step, and what Mercury records today. Based on OpenTelemetry's GenAI agent spans and a code review.

item.title: Running an agent overnight: what breaks first
item.description: We read Mercury's scheduler and budget code and reproduced one behaviour to find what fails in long unattended runs: skipped tasks and quiet errors.

item.title: How Optimus works: an agent that uses your computer
item.description: Inside Optimus, the Mercury plugin that sees your screen, moves the mouse and types: its processes, how it looks and acts, voice control, and the safety rails.

item.title: Mercury 1.4: plugins, WhatsApp calls, and Optimus
item.description: Mercury 1.4 adds isolated plugins, WhatsApp chat with voice calls both ways, and Optimus, which sees your screen and uses your mouse.

item.title: AI coding's bottleneck is verification, not generation
item.description: A Harvard working paper finds coding agents raised output while review time rose 49%. Why verification should decide whether an agent is useful.

item.title: Agents exceeded their permissions: how to scope them
item.description: CERT-In says AI agents read live business records at Indian firms. Here is how least privilege, scoped access, approvals and audit logs should limit them.

item.title: Mercury Bots: an agent fleet that runs on your machine
item.description: How Mercury Bots work, what we measured, how they compare with other always-on agents, and the commits behind them, as the work was done.

item.title: The setup wizard that quit at the first menu
item.description: A new Mercury install asked for your name, showed one menu, then quit with no error. How a one-tick race caused it, and the test that stops it returning.

item.title: We were running Mercury twice and didn't know it
item.description: Typing felt sluggish everywhere. The cause was a second full copy of the agent, started quietly by the launcher. How we found it and fixed it.

item.title: Mercury 1.3: an agent you can actually leave running
item.description: Mercury 1.3's shared background runtime, bots that deliver real files and stay online, and a fleet you run from Telegram. What changed and why.

item.title: Asks before it acts: how Mercury's permission model works
item.description: How Mercury's permission model works: scopes, approvals, a blocklist nothing overrides, an SSRF guard, and the limits that apply to unattended bots.
